Answer: B
Reason: The pre-lavage image (Figure 1a) shows dense perihilar opacities with a sharp demarcation from the normal peripheral lung parenchyma (the "crazy-paving" pattern of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis). Post-lavage (Figure 2a), these opacities have significantly decreased in size and density, but the characteristic sharp border between the remaining affected area and the clear lung tissue remains pronounced.
